metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.50 or lower) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then apply mean reversion toward 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.70+) and model forecasts are below recent low, model underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–7 day) volatility in high-sentiment periods — smooth 3-day moving average before forecasting.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., -0.50 → 0.70), model often lags — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply gradual upward correction.
- In absence of official events, model tends to overfit recent trends — apply 30-day exponential smoothing to dampen noise.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75.00), model often forecasts higher — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
